A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure shorten the time from first symptom to treatment start for lung cancer patients, and by how much?
Measure: Nurse navigator for every suspected lung cancer. A named nurse books and chases every test, calls the patient, prepares the MDT and removes waiting between steps from referral to first treatment.
effect_summary_en: A 2026 scoping review of 13 studies found that navigation was consistently linked with a faster start of first treatment, but its abstract gives no pooled number of days saved compared with care without navigation.
supported_en: The 2026 scoping review in the Japan Journal of Nursing Science (13 studies) says navigation sped up the start of first treatment through better scheduling and coordination.
not_supported_en: The review does not show the 15% (0–30%) cut in waiting time that our model assumes.
in_use_summary_en: No public sign was found of a named nurse navigator for suspected lung cancer on Lapha's lung clinic page or on OYS's lung cancer care-pathway and cancer centre pages; OYS runs the multidisciplinary meetings and the Northern Cancer Centre coordinates cancer care in the region.
summary_en: Lapha's lung clinic page lists only ordinary doctor and nurse appointments. OYS's care-pathway page says the university hospital runs the lung cancer multidisciplinary meetings, and OYS's cancer centre page says the Northern Cancer Centre coordinates cancer care in the region; none of these pages describes a nurse navigator. A 2026 scoping review of 13 studies links navigation with a faster start of treatment but gives no pooled number of days saved.
unanswered_en: I found no page that names a lung cancer coordinator nurse (syöpäkoordinaattori) or a navigation project in Lapha or OYS, and no study that measures how much time navigation saves for lung cancer.
